2.1: 2.1 Solomon determined to build a house, etc. BEDE, Questions on the Book of Kings, vol. 2. The house which Solomon built, etc., down to who prepare themselves for the building of God by believing, working, teaching others. Solomon. By both name and most peaceful reign he signifies him, etc., down to and of the enlightening of the Holy Spirit.
2.8: 2.8 And they shall be servants. RABANUS. My apostles and first teachers, etc., down to and therefore they have overcome the more subtly.
2.14: 2.14 The son of a woman. He shows that he was of the progeny of Shelomith, of the tribe of Dan, of whom it is read in the book of Numbers. The Hebrews hand down that his father was a Hebrew, of the stock of Oholiab, of the tribe of Dan, who worked with Bezalel in the wilderness. As to his calling him a Tyrian, the Hebrews say this came about through translation. For Zochri in their language is interpreted psalmody. For Chyros, which they call Zor, signifies now narrowness, now molding. Who knows how to work in gold and silver. In all these Hiram the spiritual knows how to work, that the adornment of the house of God may shine with fitting beauty before the eyes of men, and by the odor of good repute become acceptable to God.
2.16: 2.16 But we, etc. RABANUS. It signifies that the Gentiles, the fame of the Gospel having been heard, send various persons through faith to baptism. Yet it belongs to the true peacemaker alone to unite them to the unity of the Church by absolving sins through the sacraments of baptism, of whom it is said: He upon whom you shall see the Spirit descending and remaining, this is he who baptizes, Matthew 3.
2.17: 2.17 He numbered therefore, etc. There were workmen of the house of the Lord of the children of Israel, etc. RABANUS, down to build up the Church of Christ by living and teaching rightly. Three thousand six hundred. In Chronicles, for the three thousand three hundred overseers who are numbered in Kings, three thousand six hundred are written, for the perfection of lofty men. In the number six God completed the adornment of the world: and because holy Scripture teaches the faith of the Trinity and the works of righteousness, rightly three thousand six hundred are said to have been.
3.1: 3.1 In the threshing floor of Ornan. RABANUS. The Church is signified by a threshing floor, etc., down to but when Christ looked upon it, it found in him both the place and the name of peace.
3.2: 3.2 In the second month, etc. That is May, namely soon after Pascha, that the people, consecrated by the mystic solemnity, might worthily undertake the mystic work. In the fourth year of his reign. After the dispensation of the divine incarnation, which is written in the four Gospels, was fulfilled, the Spirit being sent from heaven, the Church was built. What we have expounded in the books of Kings, we treat briefly in Chronicles. The length of the house signifies the long patience of the Church. The breadth, the charity by which it loves even enemies, until it rejoices in God with friends alone. The height, the hope of the life to come and of recompense, because it despises all adversities: until it sees the goods of the Lord in the land of the living. It is to be noted that the thirty cubits of height read in Kings reached not to the roof of the temple but to the lower upper chamber. For here the height was one hundred and twenty cubits. Thirty are counted to the middle chamber, others to the third, then up to the highest roof of the temple, another thirty, and so the whole height of the house is completed in one hundred and twenty cubits: the number of persons in which the primitive Church in Jerusalem received the grace of the Holy Spirit. For fifteen, which consists of seven and eight, signifies the life to come, which is now lived in the rest of souls and will be perfected in the resurrection of bodies: and fifteen drawn into a triangle, that is, counted with all its parts, becomes one hundred and twenty, by which is designated the future blessedness of the elect. Well is the third chamber of the house completed by this number, which after present labors, after the rest of souls, is fulfilled in the full glory of happiness at the resurrection.
3.4: 3.4 And the porch, etc. Namely the temple itself, which was before the doors of the oracle: for the division of the building was threefold: that is, the porch before the temple: and the temple itself in which were the altar of incense, the table of proposition, and the lampstand: and the oracle, that is, the Holy of Holies, where the ark of the covenant and the cherubim were placed behind the veil. The porch before the temple bears the figure of the faithful of old. The temple itself, of those who came into the world after the Lord's incarnation. The inner house, the joys of the heavenly kingdom given to both. It is therefore to be noted that the walls of the house were made of precious stones, covered with cypress or cedar boards, clothed with plates of gold. Hence in Kings: And all the house was covered with cedar, etc. The stones of the wall or pavement, the boards and the gold signify the life of the saints in the Church. The living stones are the saints, joined into one rule by the strength of faith. The cedar or cypress boards also are the saints, joined to one another in the same faith by the breadth of various virtues according to the gift of the Holy Spirit. The plates of gold are the saints having the surpassing charity of knowledge, and rejoicing together by its most pleasing brightness.
3.6: 3.6 He also paved the floor, etc. As the breadth of the wall rising on high and reaching the ceiling signifies the progress of the virtues by which the saints reach heaven, or the choirs of saints succeeding one another through various times: so the evenness of the pavement signifies their harmonious humility, by which, placed in this life, they live together in social charity. The pavement laid with precious marble of great beauty, and the marble covered with fir boards, because the life of the just is first to be fortified in the heart by the firmness of faith: then adorned in work by the breadth of virtues. For what does the beauty of the marble profit when covered with boards, unless it show something mystical? But it signifies that the amplitude of good works must be supported by the strength of faith. The fir, tall and durable, shows the mind of the elect despising the lowest things, clinging to the heavenly, and excelling in the virtue of patience. The plates of gold laid over the marble on the fir boards are the breadth of charity from a pure heart and good conscience and faith unfeigned, which shines before the other virtues in the temple of God as gold before other metals.
3.7: 3.7 The beams and walls, etc. He covered them when, the Lord himself opening the entrance of faith, he shows with what truth it shines forth to all entering the Church. The door of the temple is Christ, through whom one comes to the Father, who says: I am the door, etc., John 10. In Kings it is written thus: The oracle had twenty cubits in length, and twenty in breadth, and twenty in height, 3 Kings. The oracle is called the Holy of Holies, because there secrets are revealed to men by divine and angelic speech. Hence: The oracle was made in the hidden places, that is, in the inner house, because in the heavenly country the vision and speech of angels and the very presence of God will be revealed. That he says twenty cubits of height signifies the cedar wall which separates the oracle from the outer house. He carved cherubim. This house has, as is read in Kings, projecting carvings, since the saints do not perform the works of virtue in secret but set an example before all.
3.8: 3.8 He made also the house, etc. The oracle where the ark was had twenty cubits in length, breadth and height, that is, was a perfect square: because in the heavenly country, where the saints see the king in his beauty, charity alone of divine and heavenly grace shines through all. Hence in what follows: He overlaid it with plates of gold, 3 Kings, that is, he filled the walls of the heavenly city with the grace of charity. Six hundred talents, etc. In the talents is the perfection of weight, which expresses the perfection of charity, as the perfection of six, by which a hundred is multiplied, so that they become six hundred.
3.9: 3.9 And the nails also. RABANUS. In the number fifty the remission of sins, etc., down to who, coming to more perfect things, says of the nails of perfection: But it is good for me to adhere to God, Psalm 72. The upper chambers also. As the Holy of Holies, where the ark was, signifies the inner life of the saints in the sight of the Redeemer, whence: You shall hide them in the secret of your face from the disturbance of men, Psalm 30. So the upper chambers on high signify that the same life is in heaven and not in this world, whence: Seek the things that are above, Colossians 3, where Christ is sitting at the right hand of God.
3.10: 3.10 He made also. RABANUS. This is read more fully in Kings, etc., down to to be rewarded with the denary of the everlasting kingdom.
3.11: 3.11 So that the wing. The one wing of the cherub was of five cubits, etc., because the angels keep the law of God, written in five books, with untiring devotion, namely by loving God with all their strength and their neighbors as themselves. For the fulfilling of the law is charity, Romans 13. Neighbors to one another also are the angelic spirits and the elect men. Hence both wings of the cherub are of the same measure: because with the same devotion with which they love one another in God, they also desire the fellowship of us ascending to them. Likewise therefore the wings fill up ten cubits, when the angels rejoice in the presence of their Maker in the twofold display of charity.
3.12: 3.12 They touched the wall. They touch two walls equally with their wings, because they have with them Jews and Gentiles as possessors of the heavenly court: not that there is a local distinction between the two peoples there, but because the festival of inward blessedness is greater from the fellowship of a brotherhood united in God. They extend their wings therefore to each wall: because rejoicing in the heavenly country they stir up the just of both peoples to the praise of the Creator. They extend wings covered with gold to the walls of the oracle, as they have their faces turned toward the outer house: because the angels, as they preserve their own innocence, so rejoice in the blessedness of the saints, that they bring help to those whom they still behold on earth until they lead them into the heavenly country. For they are all ministering spirits, sent to minister for them who shall receive the inheritance of salvation, Hebrews 1. With the outer wings one touches one wall, the other the other: because the Old Testament written for the ancient people, the new for us who came to the faith after the Lord's incarnation, and rightly are we compared to the second wall, that is the northern, who after the cold and darkness of idolatry have known the light of truth. His wing. They extend wings to one another over the ark, when they refer to the praise of the Savior every good they had received. They extend the other wings to the walls of the oracle, when they rejoice to see the saints with them, and as it were touch with the tips of their wings those whom they exult to have been imitators of their purity in this life. And their faces turned. Because for our sake, who still stand outside but are saved in hope, the divine books were composed, whose writers, already reigning with the Lord, take care of our salvation and intercede for us with God.
3.14: 3.14 He made also. RABANUS. This is set down earlier in Kings, etc., down to and the truth of the Gospel and the entrance of the kingdom is opened by the truth itself. And he wove in. The cherubim are woven in with these four colors when in all that we do piously we are protected from the poisoned darts of demons by angelic guards, and unceasingly use a multitude of knowledge, always looking to the divine oracles, lest we wander from the path of virtues.
3.15: 3.15 Before the doors of the temple he also made two pillars. They stood in the porch before the doors of the temple, and adorned the entrance of the temple on both sides with their beauty. The door of the temple is the Lord, who says: No one comes to the Father but by me, etc., John 14. The pillars stand round the door on both sides, when the ministers of the word show to both peoples the entrance of the heavenly kingdom, that whoever comes from the light of legal knowledge or from the error of the Gentiles to the faith of the Gospel may have them ready to show him the way of salvation by word and example. In Kings it is read of these pillars: When he came to King Solomon, he made all his work, and fashioned two pillars of bronze, etc., 3 Kings 7. Thirty-five. This number signifies the perfection of teachers. For seven multiplied by five, or five by seven, makes thirty-five. Five signifies the law; seven, on account of the sevenfold Spirit remaining in the flower of the root of Jesse, signifies the Gospel; hence elsewhere the Lord is said to have fed five thousand men with five loaves, and elsewhere four thousand with seven loaves. The pillars therefore of thirty-five cubits signify that the teachers of the Gospel have perfect knowledge of the two Testaments, whence: To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, Mark 4. And elsewhere: He opened their understanding that they might understand the Scriptures, Luke 24. As little chains. RABANUS. The manifold interweaving of the chains and the spreading of the net according to Kings thus suggests the many-sided persons of the elect, who, as they cling by faithfully listening to and obeying the words of the preachers, are like nets and little chains laid over the heads of the pillars, offering to those who behold them the marvel of their connection.
3.16: 3.16 On the heads of the pillars. The heads of the pillars, that is the topmost part, are the hearts of the teachers, by whose thoughts devoted to God, as the members by the head, all their works and words are directed. Pomegranates. One rind outside surrounds many seeds within, hence they signify the Church, because by the protection of one faith it surrounds the innumerable hosts of the elect, or the life and morals of each just man, whom, with the many ornaments of thoughts and virtues, lest perchance they flow away, the firm guard of faith and humility fences. Fitly were the heads of the pillars surrounded in a circle with pomegranates, because holy teachers call to memory the life of the faithful who went before; and by their examples confirm their sermons on every side, lest, if they lived or taught otherwise than the rule of those, they should err.
3.17: 3.17 And them also. Therefore two pillars were made and so arranged, that they may teach us to keep before our eyes, in prosperity and adversity, the entrance of the heavenly kingdom. It is to be noted that the porch of the temple is also called the vestibule, and what we read between the vestibule and the altar should be understood between the porch and the altar. The second pillar signifies the preachers who were sent to the Gentiles to preach. Or the right pillar signifies those who prophesied that the Lord would come in the flesh. The second, those who testify that he has already come and redeemed the world with his blood. Both pillars are named with a like word, when one is called firmness and the other strength, to show that strength of faith and of work is in all teachers, and to tacitly mark the teachers of our own time, who wish to be seen and called pillars of the house of God, while having in themselves no strength of firm faith for despising the pomps of the world and desiring invisible goods, nor strength to correct, nor diligence to understand, the errors of those over whom they preside.
4.1: 4.1 He made also, etc. RABANUS. The altar of holocaust signifies those who consecrate their body and soul to God with the fire of love: whose perseverance in good work the length of the altar expresses, the breadth the amplitude in the charity of God and neighbor, the height holds out hope in the expectation of the visitation. Of twenty cubits. Twenty signifies the great perfection of untiring longanimity and sincere love, which is granted to us by the observance of both Testaments. For four times five is twenty, and there are five books of the law and four Gospels. When we come, grace enlightening, to the understanding and keeping of the law, we complete the number twenty; and the same number is in the length and breadth of the altar, when the hearts of the elect, taught by both Testaments, keep perseverance in a work of this kind even in persecutions, and the cheerfulness of love even toward their persecutors. And ten cubits. In ten is signified the hope of heavenly rewards. Hence those who labor in the vineyard of the householder are paid a denarius. Hence the altar, which signifies the elect, to signify their perpetual life is raised ten cubits.
4.2: 4.2 The sea also. RABANUS. The saving laver, etc., down to and he ought to hope for the common crown of righteousness from the Lord. It had five cubits. Because whatever we offend in sight, hearing, smell, taste or touch, all is released in baptism. But the remission of past sins is not enough unless each thereafter persists in good works. Otherwise the devil who had gone out returns more manifold, and the last state of the man becomes worse than the first. Hence he hears: A line of thirty cubits. That is, the discipline of heavenly precepts, by which we are bound back from our own wills, whence: A threefold cord is not easily broken, Ecclesiastes 4; because the observance of the commandments of God in the hearts of the saints, strengthened by faith, hope and love of the heavenly recompense, can be dissolved by no adversity.
4.3: 4.3 And ten cubits. RABANUS. The sculpture beneath the lip, etc., down to with what great misery the reprobate perished on account of their crimes.
4.4: 4.4 The hinder parts. Because by what reward the preachers are to be endowed forever is disposed by the examination of God, but is as yet hidden from us, to whom this cannot be hidden, that everyone who receives baptism unto salvation must have faith, hope and charity; nor without these three virtues can he work or enter into salvation, whence in Kings it is said: The thickness of the laver was of three fingers, 3 Kings 7. The thickness of the laver is the firmness of virtue. Of three fingers, because the reception of baptism is fortified by the strength of faith, hope and love.
4.5: 4.5 Moreover the capacity. The thickness which Josephus said was of four fingers, showing what was the size of the palm. These things signify the same. For whoever by faith, hope and charity, according to the teaching of the four Gospels, does works of righteousness, also receives the reward of eternal life. Three thousand measures. A thousand signifies perfection, because ten makes a solid square. For ten times ten make a hundred, which is as it were a square figure, but flat: but that it may rise in height and be made solid, multiply a hundred by ten, and they make a thousand. By this number is signified the stable and unconquerable, and as it were square, conscience of the just. For wherever you turn a square, it will stand. So the mind of the elect is bent from the state of uprightness by no temptation. The sea holds three thousand measures; when the sacrament of baptism, given in the faith of the Trinity, confers on those washed in it the remission of all sins.
4.6: 4.6 He also made basins. In Kings thus: He also made ten bronze lavers. One laver held forty baths. And it was four cubits. And he set each laver upon each of the ten bases, etc. The apostles and apostolic men, who are signified by the oxen carrying the sea, are also expressed by the bases prepared to carry the lavers, as the lavers themselves signify baptism, which the sea prefigured. For the priests washed in them everything they were about to offer in the holocausts. The Lord's holocaust, however, can be understood as the whole multitude of the faithful, who are baptized by him in water and fire. As therefore the priests who are washed in the sea signify those who through baptism are made sharers of the High Priest, so the holocausts express the same, when after the washing of baptism they are filled with spiritual grace. For the victim is washed in the laver when the faithful is bathed with the water of baptism. It is offered as a holocaust when, through the laying on of the bishop's hand, he receives the gift of the Holy Spirit.
4.8: 4.8 And he set five. On either side of the temple the bases of the lavers were placed, that the grace of the sacred font might be shown to be opened to both peoples. And there are five on each side, so that, as in the exposition of the sea which we have said was five cubits high, it might be shown typically that everything that had been offended through the five senses of the body is to be remitted through the laver of baptism. As therefore in the one sea set upon twelve oxen the unity of baptism is expressed, which was to be preached through the apostles throughout the whole world, so also through the two rows of lavers it is mystically shown that the Gentiles with Judea were to be brought forth into one fellowship of faith through the wave of baptism. Golden lampstands. The divine oracles, which bring forth the light of wisdom, whence: Your word is a lamp to my feet, and a light, etc., Psalm 118. Hence Solomon says: For the commandment is a lamp, and the law a light, Proverbs 6. There are twice five lampstands, because the volumes of the lawgiver are five, in which the whole series of the Old Testament also embraces the five ages of the world. Five are set on the right and five on the left: when after the Lord's incarnation the same Scripture is entrusted to both peoples; or it is shown full of evangelical figures, though it was once thought to be understood only according to the letter. And tables also. RABANUS. These tables, etc., down to whose works are set before us like saving breasts as examples of life.
4.9: 4.9 He made also the court. RABANUS. The court of the priests in the Church, etc., down to we have set forth more fully in the book of Kings according to Bede. And the great hall. Which was outside the court of the priests, into which all the people flowed together to pray or to hear the word. In the Church this signifies the life and conduct of the carnal, to whom it is said: I could not speak to you as to spiritual men, but as to carnal, etc. And the hall. Well are the carnal signified by a great hall, because the number of such in the Church is much greater than that of the perfect. But as much as they exceed in number, so much do they fall short in merit. Hence this great hall, though it holds very many, does not admit them to the service of the altar, nor even into the court of the priests, because the carnal and weak, even if on account of the merit of chaste faith and piety they belong to the lot of the elect, are yet far from those who say: I will not dare to speak of anything except what Christ has wrought through me, to win obedience from the Gentiles, by word and deed. And doors in the hall. These signify that the entrance of faith is prepared by the speech of preaching, that those who come may learn how they ought to enter the Church of God through faith in Christ and the saving sacraments, and after they have entered, how religiously they ought to live.
4.11: 4.11 And Hiram made. The caldrons receive the sacred ashes, when the faithful, with a pious mind, recall for their own safeguarding the examples and sacraments of the Lord's passion, or diligently regard the departure of the just, who after great labors of struggle rejoice without end over the prize received, so that, considering the virtues of their elders, they too may become great; whence: Considering the end of their conversation, imitate their faith. And the flesh-hooks. The flesh-hooks signify the preachers who refresh the souls of the faithful with the word of God, comparing spiritual things with spiritual, but ministering to the carnal the milk of simple doctrine: those who wish to know the sacraments of Christ in summary and receive them for imitation are filled as carnal men with the saving victim; and because it is for teachers to divide to each what is fitting, the flesh-hooks are rightly made for the priests, with which they arrange the flesh of the victims as is fitting, and bring some things to clean men, and leave others to be consumed by the fires of the altar; for some things are revealed to our lowliness for refreshment, others are open only to the knowledge of the Holy Spirit; some things in Chronicles which are explained in Kings we pass over, some we do not find explained and do not wish to go beyond the custom of our littleness. For nowhere have we expounded anything by ourselves. And the bowls. The bowls signify the broader and more open discourse of holy doctrine, which gives the draught of wisdom to the piously thirsty, and by the ministry of preachers grants fitting refreshment to those who labor piously, that they may be able to come to the fountain of eternal life, from which those who drink shall not thirst forever.
4.17: 4.17 In the clay ground. The clay earth from which the molds for casting the vessels were made signifies holy Scripture, from which we receive the rule of living well. For like clay hardened by fire, it presents the form of the Lord's vessel, how great and of what kind they ought to be; since Scripture shows us the rule of righteousness that we should follow, and the examples of the saints, who stood unconquered in all things in the fire of tribulation, that we may desire to be precious vessels in the house of the Lord. But bronze melted by fire enters the molds of clay, that it may be made a vessel fit for heavenly ministries; when, softened wholesomely by humility and by the flame of divine charity or human adversity, we enter the way of the Fathers by working well, that by running well we may come to their rewards. Nor is it always necessary for us to be confined by the rules of working well, but when the good work is completed, the palm of blessed recompense is to be hoped for. For the vessels were not always kept enclosed in the molds of clay: when they had come to perfection, the barriers of the molds being broken, they were brought forth into the light, and in the temple of the Lord were arranged each in its place. Not that the works of the saints will perish, but when they have received the crown of righteousness, the offices of laborious work will cease. In the region of the Jordan. In which Christ was baptized, who, dipped in its waters, changed the element for us into the washing away of sins. And because every baptism of the faithful by which we are consecrated to the Lord is celebrated in imitation of that baptism, the vessels of the house of the Lord were rightly made in the region of the Jordan. For we cannot otherwise become vessels of election unless, looking to his baptism, we are zealous to be washed in the life-giving river. It is to be noted that he says the vessels were made not only in the region of the Jordan but in its plain, signifying the multiplication of the faithful, which was to be not only in Judea but in the breadth of the Gentiles; whence: The fields shall rejoice and all that are in them, Psalm 95. And elsewhere: We have heard of it in Ephrathah, we found it in the fields of the wood, ibid. 131. The king therefore cast the vessels of the house of the Lord in the plain of the Jordan, because the Lord, by the baptism of salvation from which he would make vessels of mercy, filled the whole breadth of the world.
4.18: 4.18 And Solomon made. He dictated what Hiram completed in the work itself. Allegorically, however, our Redeemer prepares the adornment of the Church in the holy preachers and in all the faithful, and brings about the works of virtues, who says: Without me you can do nothing, John 15; and elsewhere: Every best gift and every perfect gift is from above, etc., James 1.
4.19: 4.19 The golden altar. The hearts of the perfect shining with the light of inward charity and chastity, whose loftiness the very place of the altar also signifies. For it stood before the door of the Holy of Holies, as we read in the making of the tabernacle, on which not the blood of victims nor libations but only incense was burned, whose smoke, rising above, covered the ark and filled the oracle with the odor of sweetness. In this the saints are prefigured, who, neglecting the desires of temporal things, seek heavenly things with their whole intention, and are as though placed inside next to the oracle: nor are they far removed from the veil by which the temple and the Holy of Holies are divided; because they dwell on earth only in body, but are in heaven with the whole mind. The smoke of the incense rises from this altar within the Holy of Holies where the ark is laid up; so that the prayers of the saints, stirred by the flame of charity, may reach heaven, where Christ sits at the right hand of God. For on this altar not the blood of victims but only incense is burned, because such men have not the works of flesh and blood to slay for the Lord on the altar of the heart, but offer the vows of tears and prayers for desire of the heavenly kingdom.
4.21: 4.21 And the tongs, etc. The tongs for the use of the altar were made of bronze. But also those with which the lamps were cleansed signify the interpretation of the spiritual sense through the offices of the teachers. For they, passing the very words of the sacred utterance from history to allegory, from shadow to truth, multiply the light of knowledge in the Church, as though set upon the mystic lampstand.
4.22: 4.22 And he carved the doors. These are the teachers and priests who, by instructing, baptizing, and communicating the mysteries of the Lord's body and blood, open to us the first thresholds of the Church. And so everything was completed. When the true Peacemaker on the last day glorifies all the elect with the immortality of the resurrection. As long as the state of this age continues, Solomon does indeed do the work of the house of the Lord, but does not perfect it: because the Lord inspires and helps the hearts of the elect to do good, yet grants no one to be without sin, which he reserves for the faithful in the future. He perfects the whole work of his temple and makes it fit for dedication when he leads the elect, translated from this life, to the eternal kingdom: hence it is built in seven years, and in the eighth is dedicated complete. For all time revolves in seven days; the eighth is the day of judgment and resurrection, to which what follows is fitting.
5.1: 5.1 Solomon therefore brought in all, etc. RABANUS. This is done when Christ, etc., down to but there are many mansions in it for receiving all whom the Lord blesses who fear him and love him, the little with the great.
5.9: 5.9 But the bars. THE SAME. It is to be noted that, etc., down to so much the less do they see the inner joys.
5.10: 5.10 And there was nothing else. He shows in general that there was nothing in the ark contrary to the law of the Lord contained in the two tables; but there were laid up there only those things which were done typically according to the commandments of the law for the worship of one God and the commendation of our faith, that the shadow of things to come might in all things bear witness to the truth to come, and receive its end when it appeared in the world. There was, however, in the ark, according to Paul, a golden urn holding the manna, because in the man Christ dwells all the fullness of divinity bodily. There was also the rod of Aaron, which, cut off, had blossomed again: because all power of judging is with him, whose judgment seemed to be taken away in the humility of the passion. There were also the tables of the testament, because in him are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge. And the staves by which it was carried were attached, because the teachers who once labored in the word of Christ now rejoice together in the present sight of the glory of Christ. Hence: I desire to be dissolved and to be with Christ, Philippians 1.
5.12: 5.12 Clothed in fine linen. By the linen robes the white purity of bodily chastity is signified: with this are clothed all who stand in the service of God and sound his praises with mouth, conduct, and deed. For the cymbals signify the confession of the mouth, the psalteries mortality, the harps the mortification of the flesh and the vigor of good action, furnished with twenty-four strings, that is, with prophetic and apostolic teachings. Priests. Or teachers, namely expressed by the hundred and twenty, because the lawgiver completed the sum of his years in this number, and on the day of Pentecost those who believed received the grace of the Paraclete Spirit in the same number.
5.13: 5.13 Therefore all. RABANUS. All the priests and Levites, etc., down to they have lost the ministry of the true priesthood.
5.14: 5.14 For it had filled. Because the mysteries which lay hidden under a veil were opened by the coming of Christ to believers and to those worthily receiving them. But to the rest, unwilling to come to the faith, the former blindness remained. Hence: To you it is given to know the mystery of the kingdom of God, etc., Matthew 13.
6.1: 6.1 In the thick darkness. Hence Job: The clouds are his hiding place, Job 22. And the Psalmist: Darkness is under his feet: and he made darkness his hiding place, Psalm 17. The hiding place of the Lord is sacred Scripture, which carries heavenly sacraments under parables and figures. Hence: I confess to you, Lord, Father of heaven and earth, because you have hidden these things from the wise and prudent, and have revealed them to little ones, Matthew 11.
7.5: 7.5 He dedicated. RABANUS. Christ cleansed it with his blood, and sanctified it by spiritual grace, and multiplied it with the various gifts of virtues. And the children of Israel dedicate it, because each of the faithful, according to the gift conferred on him by God, converts and advances his neighbors to better and more perfect things by word and example.
7.7: 7.7 He sanctified. Because Christ perfects in the Church the things that in the law could not be perfected on account of its weakness. For the Church itself is the court of the house of the Lord, through which entrance lies open into the heavenly Jerusalem: since therefore holocausts and sacrifices could not be offered on the altar of the Old Testament, because everything there was done figuratively, our king and priest raised up a new altar of faith in the Church, on which they daily offer fat holocausts and sacrifices acceptable to God. Hence: The sacrifice of praise will honor me, and there is the way, etc.
7.8: 7.8 He kept therefore. RABANUS. I do not think this is to be understood otherwise, etc., down to in the future rest of souls, in the reception of the truth itself in the reality.
7.10: 7.10 Therefore on the day, etc. That is, after the eighth day of the solemnity of tabernacles: as is contained in Kings. It signifies, however, that after the end of that life, and after the sabbath of the holy souls, in which they rest before the judgment, in the eighth age, that is, on the day of the resurrection, the saints will receive immortal bodies, and be placed in the heavenly mansions according to the quality of their merits, where they will always rejoice, praising God for all the goods which the Father has conferred in Christ upon the Christian people.
8.1: 8.1 And when the twenty years were completed, etc., which Hiram had given, etc. RABANUS in Chronicles, from Jerome. He had returned them, namely, because when Solomon had given them they did not please him. Therefore Solomon assigned them to his own uses.
8.5: 8.5 Beth-horon. RABANUS. It is a city, as far as which Joshua pursued the enemy kings, in the tribe of Ephraim, etc., down to and another lower Beth-horon, given to the Levites for a possession.
8.6: 8.6 And all. Ezer, namely, Megiddo and Gezer and Millo, all of which show the beauty of the Church: because the true Solomon in the joy of his kingdom prepared them for praise and gladness for himself. Millo is interpreted fulfillment; Ezer, separated and sanctified; Megiddo, his cenacle; Gezer, cutting off or division; Beth-horon, house of mountains; Baalath, ascending. Holy Church is the city of the living God, where the will of God is daily fulfilled, and, separated from every error of unbelievers, is sanctified by faith and good work. There is the refreshment of the virtues. She discerns the clean from the unclean, and vice from virtue: and she is the house of mountains, that is, the dwelling of the saints, and flourishing with the fruit of righteousness like a palm, she ascends from virtue to virtue, that she may see the God of gods in Zion, Psalm 83. Solomon fortified all his towns, because Christ so fortifies the assembly of his faithful by the protection of his grace that they can resist their spiritual enemies. In Lebanon. JEROME. In the temple, namely, which was clothed with the beauty of cedars, hence Zechariah: Open your doors, O Lebanon, Zechariah 11; or in the royal buildings which were made of the wood of Lebanon.
8.10: 8.10 Two hundred. The hundred, which in the counting of the fingers passes from the left hand to the right, signifies eternal life. The fifty, however, signifies the remission of sins, and eternal rest, and the grace of the Holy Spirit: because in the psalm of the same number repentance, confession, and remission of sins are described; and through the jubilee the rest to come. Through Pentecost, however, in the coming of the Holy Spirit the sevenfold grace is expressed. Who taught. Because he chose from both peoples the rulers of the Church, who, enlightened by spiritual grace and fully taught, would teach by their own example that the remission of sins, and the life of eternal salvation, and perpetual blessedness are to be sought.
8.12: 8.12 Holocausts. RABANUS. A holocaust is said to be wholly burnt; this is burned on the altar when in the heart of every elect person who has vowed himself wholly, namely in flesh and heart, to God, the good work is kindled with the fervent fire of charity.
8.14: 8.14 He arranges everything in the Church according to the fitness of each time, that each order, performing its office, may minister worthily.
8.17: 8.17 In Ezion-geber. It is said to be an island not far from Elath on the Red Sea, where the fleet of Jehoshaphat perished. RABANUS. The fleet which Solomon made, etc., down to they find through the grace of the Holy Spirit, and ascribing divine things to his wisdom and counsel they give them to him.
8.18: 8.18 In Ophir. Ophir is the name of a province, called from one of the descendants of Eber, of whose stock Josephus relates that those who came from the river Cophen dwelt as far as the region of India which is called Geria.
9.1: 9.1 And the queen. RABANUS in Chronicles, vol. 3. The queen of the south, who, roused from the ends of the earth, came to hear the wisdom of Solomon, prefigured the Church of the Gentiles about to come to Christ: who, clothed about with variety in a gilded garment, forgetting her people and her father's house, was barbarian in nation, not in mind, because she desired to become a fellow citizen of the saints, whence: The queen of the south shall rise in judgment with this generation, Matthew 12.
9.3: 9.3 And after she had, etc. These things suit the Church, which, having heard the miracles of Christ, was moved to seek him. But after she came to him through baptism and faith, considering the testimonies of Scripture she recognized the presence of the divinity, and what she had heard of him before seemed little to her in comparison with the grace received. Hence in admiration she bursts into his praise, saying: Blessed are your men, etc.
9.12: 9.12 Of the wood. Christ places precious woods, that is, the holy teachers, whose greenness of faith never withers, nor do the leaves of words fall, but yield the fruit of good works in their seasons, for the defense of the house of the Lord and the house of the king, that is, for the strengthening of the Church, that fenced about on every side by their teaching and examples she may not feel ruin. These are said to be made like harps and lyres for praising the Lord, because whatever they do shall prosper, and they proclaim the praise of the Lord in prosperity and adversity with heart and mouth and work, and do all things to the glory of God, and all the day and night do not cease to praise the name of the Lord.
9.13: 9.13 Six hundred. Six multiplied by six makes thirty-six. And a hundred taken six times gives six hundred. Ten signifies the perfection of the commandments, a hundred the recompense of eternal blessedness. For our King desires our perfection, that he may have those to whom to give the perfect reward, whence: Be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect. If you wish to enter into life, keep the commandments, Matthew 5, 19. And a little after: If you wish to be perfect, go, sell all you have, etc., and everyone who has left house, etc., shall receive a hundredfold and possess eternal life. And all the kings of Arabia. Diverse nations and merchants and all the kings of Arabia and the governors of the lands offer to Solomon gold and silver: because every nation and every person, each according to strength, vies in offering to our Peacemaker the gift of right faith, purity of sense, fullness of holy confession, brightness of eloquence, whence: The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall offer gifts, etc. And all kings shall adore him, all nations shall serve him, Psalm 71.
9.15: 9.15 He made therefore. Because the fathers of both Testaments, perfect in teaching and working, proved by deed whatever they taught in word. Golden spears. This is the armor of God, by which we resist the snares of the devil: holy preachers have it, who guard the house of God, and keep watch at its door, lest the ancient enemy enter, whence: Sixty valiant men surround the bed of Solomon, Proverbs 3.
9.16: 9.16 Three hundred also. It signifies perfect faith in the confession of the holy Trinity. Well do the guardians of the house of God carry golden spears and shields: because the preachers, who are the guardians of the Church, shining with the brightness of wisdom, pierce enemies with the darts of words, and with the shield of faith quench the most wicked fiery darts. Six also little arms. In the number six is the perfection of good works. For in six days God made the world, and six is the first perfect number. By good and perfect works heaven is ascended. A golden footstool. The saints shining with the splendor of virtues, in whom God dwells. By the footstool may also be marked those who are weak in the body of Christ, such as penitents, or those who will be converted last, near the end of the world, who nevertheless are golden, refined and proved by the fire of the tribulation of that time. Standing beside the little arms: and twelve other little lions, etc. Because the holy Fathers ascribed whatever good they did in the Gospel not to themselves but to God, whence: Not to us, Lord, not to us, but to your name give glory, Psalm 113. Little arms, etc. In Kings thus: And two hands on either side holding the seat, 3 Kings 10. These are the solaces of divine grace, which advance the Church to the heavenly kingdom. Or this is designated by the number two, because in both Testaments this is especially commended, that nothing good can be perfected except by divine help. Hence: Without me you can do nothing, John 5.
9.19: 9.19 Six steps. Because they strive by teaching and example, that the labor of the foolish may not waver in working, but strongly preserve uprightness in the progress of the virtues. There was not such a throne, etc. Because it is written of the Church: Strength and beauty are her clothing, etc., 3 Kings 10. And: Many daughters have gathered riches: you have surpassed them all, Proverbs 31.
9.20: 9.20 And all. The souls of the saints who serve the will of God, shining with the splendor of wisdom and charity, contain the drink of living water, which becomes in them a fountain of water springing up to eternal life, John 4. Silver. The word of God is not in speech but in power, as in the preaching of the Gospel; not in persuasive words of human wisdom, but in the demonstration of spirit and power.
9.21: 9.21 For the king's ships went to Tarshish, etc. RABANUS. Christ sends the apostles, the teachers of the Gospel whom he chose from the Jews, together with the preachers chosen from the Gentiles, into the world with a threefold confession but one faith, that they may bring to him from believers the gold of wisdom, the silver of eloquence, and the ivory of chastity. The ape, however, is an ingenious animal, and an imitator of man, and can signify the philosophers, who sometimes change the senses of true wisdom, and in their disciplines discuss the acts of the moral life. The peacock, which displays its praised feathers, signifies those who for the praises of men make a show of the kinds of various virtues; but those instructed by the doctrine of the preachers learn to do well with regard to God alone, and are fitted for the delights of the eternal king.
9.25: 9.25 Forty. Forty signifies the times of the ancient law. For Moses, about to receive the law, fasted forty days, and the people instructed through him went around the wilderness forty years. Six, however, signifies the present time, in which the apostolic teaching of the New Testament nourishes the people. Well therefore are the horses of Solomon placed in stalls counted by forty, because by the hardness of the old law the insolence of the former people was restrained. Twelve signifies the present time, in which apostolic authority nourishes the people of the Gentiles with the teaching of the New Testament. In Jerusalem. In the vision of peace. The distance of places shows the difference of affections. For those who are in the cities of the chariots signify those who are instructed by spiritual masters in the various disciplines of the Church. Others, already instructed and fitted for the use of the heavenly King, deserve to have his presence. Hence: The chariot of God is ten thousand fold, etc., Psalm 76. And elsewhere: Mounting upon your horses, and your riding is salvation, Habakkuk 3. Of the Philistines. Of those falling doubly. For Philistim is interpreted double ruin. This is done when through the absolution of sins, from its beginning in the baptism of the Jordan until the conversion of all nations to the faith of Christ, the grace of power overflows, so that where there was a flowing away of carnal desires, there the shoot of virtues may be established; and where idolatry and the shameful conduct of peoples was a double ruin, there through the confession of right faith and the worship of piety the life of the faithful may rise to the heavenly kingdom. For his power reaches to the borders of Egypt, that is, the dark minds of unbelievers, which it fills with the light of faith; hence: Before him the Ethiopians shall fall down, etc.
9.27: 9.27 And so great. The true Solomon provides in the Church an abundance of silver like stones, when he turns the insensible hearts of the Gentiles, to the knowledge of the true God, those who worshiped stones for God, to the meditation of the law and the preaching of the Gospel. Of whom it is said: Those who make them become like them, etc., Psalm 113. And elsewhere: God is able from these stones to raise up children to Abraham, Matthew 3. He provides also a multitude of cedars like sycamores, because he advanced the barrenness of the Gentiles, who were unwilling to lift themselves on high, to fruitfulness of good works and virtues. And of cedars. The cedar is of incorruptible nature, pleasant in smell, bright in appearance, which when kindled puts serpents to flight and destroys them with its brightness. But the rest. Which he did after he transgressed the law of God, when foreign wives drew him on even to idolatry: many indeed like Solomon begin well and end badly, and no one ought to be called blessed before death and the last funeral.
10.8: 10.8 He forsook the counsel of the old men, etc. JEROME. The Hebrews say this was Benaiah the son of Jehoiada and Jehiel the son of Hachmoni, who is also called Chilla: whose counsel being forsaken, Rehoboam began to take counsel with the young men, that is, Adoram, who in what follows is said to have been stoned, and the like. We often call a man young not by age but by mind. For Rehoboam was not young in age but in sense: who began to reign in the forty-first year of his age.
10.13: 10.13 And the king answered, etc. This signifies the bad rulers in the Church, who, given to earthly desires, neglect the care of their subjects, and rejoice in the multitude of those who serve them. Rehoboam is interpreted breadth of the people. These are they who enter the broad way that leads to death, not the narrow that leads to life; and, forsaking the counsel of the fathers whose words and deeds tend to the height of perfection, choose to obey the counsel of the young, who burden them with praises and flatteries, who are blind and leaders of the blind, etc., whence: Woe to you, O land, whose king is a child, etc., Ecclesiastes 10.
11.21: 11.21 He loved, etc. He had, however, eighteen wives joined to him by law, and thirty concubines. And eighteen sons were born to him, and sixty daughters.
12.2: 12.2 In the fifth year of King Rehoboam, he went up. RABANUS. Bad rulers by their negligence provoke the prince of darkness against the Church, who carries off the treasures of the house of the Lord and the treasures of the king, when he takes away the knowledge of the Scriptures and the works of virtues from the incautious and the slothful.
12.9: 12.9 Shishak king. Linen of sackcloth, or joy of sackcloth. Linen indeed signifies subtlety; sackcloth, which is made of goats' hair, sins. In the linen of sackcloth, therefore, the cunning of devilish fraud in the persuasion of sin. Shishak carries off the riches of Jerusalem, when the devil, who deceives cunningly and rejoices in the multitude of sins, despoils ecclesiastical men of spiritual knowledge and of the work of virtue: and those who seemed an ornament in the Church, despoiled, he plunges with himself into the pit of perdition. Shields. Solomon made golden shields, and gave them to the guardians of his house, when Christ entrusted spiritual knowledge through the two Testaments to the teachers of the Church for the protection of the people. The ancient enemy through carelessness drags this backward. For when they attend to earthly things and care less for heavenly ones, he leaves them stripped of their former office and knowledge, as though despoiled of riches in their own house. But such, when they see themselves deprived of the spiritual sense, seek an abundance of words through eloquence, whose sounding they set against enemies on behalf of their subjects like the firmness of bronze shields. But as much as bronze is cheaper than gold, so much is eloquence inferior to the fruit of true wisdom. Hence: Where there are many words, there is often want, Proverbs 14.
12.15: 12.15 Shemaiah. Who above rebuked Rehoboam and the sons of Judah for their sins. Iddo. Who is also Abdo; this is he who was sent by the Lord to Samaria to rebuke Jeroboam for the altar he had made, who was killed on the way because, against the Lord's command, he was seduced by a false prophet and ate there.
13.4: 13.4 Samaria. RABANUS, from Jerome. It is a city which Joshua took, its king being killed, which they say is now called Sebaste, a town of Palestine, where the relics of John the Baptist are laid. We read, however, in Kings that Omri king of Israel bought the hill of Samaria from one Shemer, and built a city on its top, which he named Samaria after the name of its lord, namely Shemer.
13.19: 13.19 Bethel. RABANUS. A city at the next stone from Aelia, on the right of those going to Neapolis, which was first called Luz, that is Almond, and fell in the lot of Benjamin near Beth-aven and Ai, which Joshua stormed, its king being killed. Ephron. A city in the tribe of Judah. Hence a very large village Ephrea toward the north at the twentieth milestone from Aelia is so called to this day.
13.20: 13.20 In the days. Not of Jeroboam, in whose twentieth year, according to the book of Kings, Asa the son of Abijah reigned over Judah and Jerusalem, but Abijam, who, having taken Bethel, kept the idols for Israel as a scandal, as the Hebrews assert.
14.2: 14.2 He went out, etc. When Azariah had reigned ten years, Zerah king of Ethiopia moved his camp against him with an exceedingly great army, leading ninety thousand foot and ten thousand horse, and three hundred chariots. His camp being pitched against him, when Asa saw the multitude of the Ethiopians, he asked victory of God with a great cry, and that he himself might destroy so many thousands of men. For he said that confidence was to be placed in no other than in him who could show even a few stronger than many, and make the weak prevail over the strongest.
15.15: 15.15 But Azariah, etc. The prophet Azariah, meeting them, commanded them to stay their journey a little from the road, and then began to tell them that the victory had been granted them by God because they had kept themselves just and holy and done all things by the will of God. He said that, continuing in his commandments, they would prevail over their enemies, and by divine power have happiness and prosperity; but that forsaking religion they would come to the contrary, and that a time would come in which no true prophet would be found among that people, nor priest, on account of which the cities would be overthrown, and the nation scattered through every land, and they would have a miserable and needy life.
17.3: 17.3 He walked in the ways of David, etc. RABANUS. He shows that he was, like David, a doer of the divine commandments before he sinned with the wife of Uriah, whose satisfaction for that sin obtained for him eternal memory.
17.5: 17.5 All Judah gave gifts to Jehoshaphat. This signifies the faithful from the Gentiles, who, forsaking the error of the fathers, come together to Christ, washed with baptism, anointed with chrism, receiving from Christ the Christian name and royal dignity. Hence: You are a chosen race, a royal priesthood, etc., 1 Peter 2. For in the time of Jehoshaphat, the dowry of the Lord, either who is the dowry, or who is endowed, and because the Church of the Gentiles, purchased by the blood of Christ, given the pledge of the Holy Spirit, has deserved the fellowship of the heavenly Bridegroom and a share in the kingdom. To whom infinite riches were made when diverse nations believe, and in the acquisition of diverse virtues.
17.10: 17.10 And so there was fear, etc. By the virtues that are wrought in the Church, the boldness of the Gentiles is taken away, and they are stirred up to bring to Christ the gifts of faith and the tribute of good work, and of pious confession, and the flocks of simplicity.
18.2: 18.2 And he went down, etc. These are the heresiarchs who lead the throng of the lost through the byways of errors, and plunge them into the precipice of death. Jehoshaphat was joined in affinity with Ahab, and went down to him in Samaria against the enemies to help him: and he signifies those who from Catholics incline to friendship with heretics: who, though they do not depart from the path of right faith, yet do not avoid the society and communion of those in error. Against whom it is said: A heretical man, after the first and second admonition, avoid, Titus 3. Hence Jehoshaphat is rebuked through Jehu the seer, son of Hanani, of that prophet, namely, who had rebuked Asa, since he had offered help to the wicked, and was joined in friendship with those who hate the Lord. GREGORY, book II of the Morals, ch. 15, vol. 1. The throne of the Lord is the angelic powers, etc., down to and he would be found the more harshly to punishment, the more securely he lived in guilt.
19.10: 19.10 Every cause that shall come to you, etc. AUGUSTINE, book IV of the City of God, ch. 3. Justice being removed, what are kingdoms but great robberies? since robberies themselves, what are they but small kingdoms?
20.1: 20.1 Of the Ammonites. He signifies the Idumeans, but the writer of the history preferred to mark what was done by the name of their allies rather than publicly divulge the impiety of the shameless.
20.2: 20.2 From these places, etc. He means those places which are beyond the Salt Sea, which is otherwise called the lake of Asphaltites or the Dead Sea. Engedi. A very large village of the Jews near the Dead Sea is called so to this day, whence the balsam comes: which Solomon calls the vineyards of Engedi.
20.16: 20.16 For they will come up by the slope called Ziz, etc. RABANUS in Chronicles, from Jerome. Which is also Jeruel according to the Hebrews. For they say that Ziz, etc., down to fear of foreigners was struck on every side. Mystically, the Moabites, Ammonites, and Edomites signify pagans, Jews, and heretics, who freely stir up war against the faithful and strive to take away the Christian religion. But Jehoshaphat, that is, the people of Christ, attacks them not with bodily arms but with spiritual, seeking heavenly help with inmost devotion of heart.
20.25: 20.25 Jehoshaphat therefore came, etc. The holy teachers, with the throng of the faithful, gather from the spoils of the enemies whatever they have usefully believed from reading, writing, and teaching in physics, ethics, and logic, and turn it, through faith in the holy Trinity, to the use of the whole Church, that what they possessed unjustly and uselessly, the faithful, possessing it usefully, may possess for the salvation of souls.
20.26: 20.26 The valley of blessing. The humility of the Church, where praises are worthily rendered to God. He who, instructed by the doctrine of the four Gospels, has come through the faith of baptism to the unity of the Church, there rightly praising, conversing worthily with God, will enter into the vision of perpetual peace with praise and everlasting gladness.
21.2: 21.2 All these were sons of Jehoshaphat, etc. RABANUS. Imitators of his works, their brother Jehoram always sliding into worse things, whence Jehoram himself is read to have killed them with the princes of Israel.
21.14: 21.14 Behold the Lord will strike you, etc. Through the Philistines and Arabs who laid waste his land, and plundered the substance and likewise the sons and wives of Jehoram, which is interpreted, Who is the exalted: who from a religious father turned aside to perfidy, and made the sons of Judah fornicate: he signifies those who, imbued with faith and regenerated by baptism, forsake the truth of faith, following the error of heretics, and perverting others with them. Hence Elijah, that is the prophetic word, rebukes them: because the whole authority of the divine books reprehends such, and deservedly rebukes their perversity with the gravest attestations.
21.20: 21.20 And he reigned eight years, etc. Of Jehoram, that he reigned eight years and lived forty; but that his son Ahaziah, when he began to reign, was forty-two years old, which if so, he begot a son two years before he himself was born. But the Hebrews say that Jehoram, who is described as having lived forty years and reigned eight, lived forty years and reigned twenty-eight. For the eight years which are assigned to him in the kingdom are those in which he reigned before he killed his brothers, when he still lived innocently. The remaining twenty years in which he afterwards reigned are not counted because he lived in sickness and tribulation: and therefore they are attributed to his son, who is held to be no more than twenty-two years old according to the book of Kings, lest the remaining years from the sum of the numbers should cause an error in the reckoning of the times.
22.6: 22.6 Azariah son of Jehoram, etc. RABANUS, from Jerome. Who above is Ahaziah, that is, laying hold of the Lord: Azariah, however, the help of the Lord. And therefore according to the Hebrews his name is changed for the better: because according to the command of the Lord he visited the sick.
22.7: 22.7 Against Jehu, etc. Jehu signifies the primacy of the Gentiles, whom Christ destined against the sacrilegious city that killed the prophets and the Lord of the prophets, and persecuted the apostles; that he might punish it with fitting vengeance, and destroy the shrine of the priests after the coming of Christ, and overthrow the temple: and might cast down from the height of the kingdom, like Jezebel, the impious synagogue thirsting for their blood, and slay its rulers.
22.10: 22.10 If indeed Athaliah, etc. Athaliah, who tried to extinguish the seed of David and to destroy the royal stock, signifies the impiety of the Synagogue, which through wickedness of mind lies in wait for the seed of Christ, raging with inexorable hatred, and which once seemed to reign while it observed the temporal ceremonies of the law. Athaliah is interpreted temporal of the Lord, but through the vigor of Jehosheba, which is interpreted fullness of the Lord, that is, of the Church in which are true delights, Joash is preserved, which is interpreted memory of the Lord, that is, Christ, in whom is the memory of the name of the Lord: lest he be destroyed in his saints by the cruelty of the raging one, but be nourished in the house of the priest Jehoiada, which is interpreted beloved of the Lord, that is Christ, of whom the Father says: This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased, Matthew 17. Whose house is the Church, where, remaining in the faith of the elect, he daily makes increase of his body, that in the time of judgment he may lift up the scepter of the kingdom and power against those who oppressed him.
23.13: 23.13 On the step. RABANUS. The column, namely, and the base, which Solomon had prepared and set in the midst of the hall, having five cubits of length, and five of breadth, and three in height.
23.16: 23.16 And Jehoiada made a covenant. Jehoiada is interpreted knowing the Lord, or loving: because he taught the children of Israel to know the Lord. He made therefore a covenant between the Lord and the people and the king, that they should obey the Lord, namely, and his law. He made also one between the king and the people, that the people should act faithfully toward the king, and the king rule the people justly according to the teaching of the priests and Levites, whose office it was to make known the commandments of the Lord.
24.4: 24.4 After which it pleased Joash, etc. RABANUS. King Joash rebukes the priests, etc., down to lest through the negligence of the teachers the multitude of hearers perish.
24.7: 24.7 And his sons, etc. Not that she then had sons, because Ahaziah being dead, since he had no son, she endeavored to kill all the royal seed, but he names her sons the priests of the idols, who had despoiled the temple, and adorned their idols with its ornaments; for imitators are often called sons.
24.12: 24.12 But they hired, etc. The apostles do this when, through disciples subject to them, they scattered the seeds of the divine word through the world, that they might set over the hearers workmen fit for the will of God: of whom some make timber, when they prepare themselves and those obedient to them as fruitful trees in the house of God. Others made repairs of the roofs, when they rebuilt those things which had been broken by heresy or schisms. Others hew stones, when they sharply rebuke the hard of heart and unbelieving. Others work metals of iron and bronze, when they require from each the strength of faith and the confession of catholic truth, that the house of God may be filled, according to that: To each of us grace is given according to the measure of Christ's gift, Ephesians 4.
24.14: 24.14 The rest of the money, etc. What is read in the book of Kings seems contrary: But there were not made from the same money cups for the temple and flesh-hooks, 4 Kings 12. But it is not said here that from the same money which was offered by the people in the temple of the Lord for the repair of the house of God the sacred vessels were made for the ministry of the temple and for the holocausts, but from the remaining part of the money, that is, from that which had been conferred by other donations. For it could be that at different times the money offered furnished the material for different works, as the doctrine with which the unlearned are imbued for the faith is one, and that with which the perfect are instructed for fullness is another.
24.18: 24.18 And wrath came. RABANUS, from Jerome. The Hebrews relate that the princes of Judah worshiped the king as God, and that he gladly accepted it: hence he greatly offended the Lord, and suddenly experienced the wrath he deserved. For this fault also Herod is read in the Acts of the Apostles to have been struck by an angel.
24.25: 24.25 Of Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, etc. RABANUS. The Lord in the Gospel, remembering Zechariah slain between the temple and the altar, etc., down to which they call Siloam, showing red rocks, they think to be polluted with the blood of Zechariah.
24.26: 24.26 And they conspired, etc. The Hebrews assert that the Ammonites and Moabites conspired against King Joash for the unjust killing of Zechariah, to heighten the malice of the Israelites, who were unwilling to avenge the priest of God, whom the sons of foreigners avenged.
25.11: 25.11 To the valley of salt, etc. RABANUS. Where salt was made, either from salt hay cut, dried and burned, as in many places, or from salt well waters boiled and brought to the firmness of salt. Or otherwise, where Joab also is read to have struck twelve thousand Edomites. For the valley of Salt the old edition put, as the name of a region, Gemel.
25.16: 25.16 I know, he said, that the Lord has planned, etc. Who wills no one to perish, but condemns by just judgment him who persists in sin. Amaziah therefore perished because, admonished by the prophet to repent, he did not obey, but continued to the end.
25.18: 25.18 The thistle that, etc. He hints at this likeness: because Amaziah, sprung from most noble birth, coming from the stock of David, living in the foulness of idolatry and become base, does not consider his own measure, but exalts himself beyond measure in the pride of arrogance.
25.21: 25.21 Beth-shemesh. RABANUS. In Kings Beth-shemesh is called a town of Judah: because it belongs to the kingdom of Judah, that is, to the two tribes which the house of David ruled; but according to the situation of the places it belongs to the tribe of Benjamin.
25.24: 25.24 And with Obed-edom, etc. Because he took away not only the vessels which he found in the house of God, but also those which the doorkeepers and guardians of the temple watched over. In Kings, however, it is read that David chose seventy-two of the sons of Obed-edom to minister in the house of God and to guard the temple.
25.27: 25.27 After he had departed. From the time he did not hear the counsel of the prophet, nor would be turned to the Lord, a conspiracy was prepared and delayed until it reached completion.
26.3: 26.3 Uzziah, when he began to reign. Who is also Azariah. Uzziah is interpreted strength of the Lord. Azariah, help of the Lord, because as long as he acted rightly, helped by divine aid he waged very many wars successfully and triumphed over his enemies. But before he attempted unlawful things through pride, struck with leprosy he clouded the dignity of his name and honor, shut out from the people until the day of his death.
26.9: 26.9 At the valley gate. RABANUS. This is the gate of Ephraim, etc., down to concerning this gate and the other gates of Jerusalem we have said abundantly in Ezra, following Bede.
26.16: 26.16 But when he was strong, etc. Uzziah was at first just, and did right in the sight of the Lord: hence he conquered his enemies and had many prophets in his rule. Hence as long as Zechariah the priest, surnamed the understanding, lived, he pleased God, serving in the temple with all reverence. But after Zechariah died, wishing to offer the gifts himself, he invaded the dignity of the priesthood not so much piously as boldly, nor did he obey the Levites and priests who cried out against it: hence he was struck with leprosy on the forehead, which the priest protected with a plate of gold, which in Ezekiel the Lord commands to be marked with the impression of the letter Tau. And entering the temple of the Lord, because, clothed in the priestly robe, at the pressing of the solemn festival he entered the temple to the golden altar, about to offer incense according to Josephus. Hence before the city in the place called Eroge, the middle part of the mountain was split to the west, and by its own rolling advancing four stadia stopped at the eastern mountain, so that it blocked the roads and oppressed the royal gardens. The Hebrews hold that this happened in the twenty-fifth year of Uzziah, whose remaining years are twenty-seven. Uzziah reigned fifty-two years, at which time Amulius ruled among the Latins and Agamestor among the Athenians; he being dead, Isaiah saw the vision, as he himself testifies, at the time, namely, when Romulus, founder of the Roman empire, was born.
26.23: 26.23 In the field of the royal tombs. Not in the royal burial places, not in the city of David. For heretics and schismatics are unworthy of the fellowship and communion of holy Church, nor is their memory held among Catholics: because, stained with errors and foul with vices, they are separated from their company.
27.1: 27.1 Jotham was twenty-five years old, etc. At the beginning and at the end he counts the years of Jotham, because as he began in righteousness, so he persevered to the end. Hence the times of his life are proclaimed as worthy of praise.
27.3: 27.3 He built the gate, etc. Which in the Acts of the Apostles is called Beautiful, and according to the Hebrews is called by them the gate of Jotham to this day because he built it. Ophel. It was a tower not far from the temple, of wonderful height. Hence Ophel received the name of darkness or cloud. Where it is written in Micah: And you, cloudy tower of the flock, daughter of Zion, Micah 4:8: in the Hebrew it is the tower of Ophel. The tower of Ophel signifies the eminence of Scripture, which, founded in history, hides the head of the spiritual sense among the clouds, while it hides the greatness of knowledge from the eyes of men. Hence: He made darkness his hiding place, Psalm 17. Jotham, whose life is praised, signifies Christ, of whom it is said: Great is the Lord and exceedingly to be praised, ibid. 47, etc. For Jotham is interpreted consummated or perfect, and of Christ the Apostle says: And being consummated, he became to all who obey him the cause of eternal salvation, etc., Hebrews 5. He built the lofty gate of the house of the Lord, and brought about the mystery of his incarnation by wonderful power, who says of himself: I am the door. By me if any man enter in, he shall be saved, John 10. This gate was called lofty, of which the Psalmist says: The Lord is high above all nations, Psalm 112, etc.
28.3: 28.3 In the valley of Ben-hinnom. RABANUS. This is the valley of Ben-hinnom, etc., down to for all adulterers, like an oven, are their hearts.
29.3: 29.3 In the very year, etc. RABANUS. He would not otherwise imitate David his father, who, devoted to God from infancy, at the beginning of his reign magnified the worship of God. Morally, however, it admonishes the rulers of the Church not to be slothful in the office committed to them, but to do all things diligently. Mystically Hezekiah, who not only by himself or by his own strenuously did the work of God, but even by messengers provoked others to like zeal, signifies Christ, as the interpretation of the name also testifies. For Hezekiah is laying hold of the Lord, or strength of the Lord. Christ is the power of God and the wisdom of God, who washed away with his blood all the transgressions of the fathers which had been under the law, and plainly restored the worship of piety in the Church. He sent envoys to call the Gentiles to the faith. First the prophets, then the apostles, and their successors: he instituted the celebration of the Passover in the second month; because the shadow of the law ceasing, he taught the true Passover to be kept, of which Paul says: For Christ our Passover is sacrificed, 1 Corinthians 5.
29.6: 29.6 Our fathers have sinned, etc. JEROME, Questions on Chronicles, vol. 3. This is written fully, etc., down to and worshiped at the rising of the sun.
30.1: 30.1 He sent also, etc. JEROME. When he had publicly sent messengers to all Israel, he sent secretly to Manasseh and Ephraim, to those he knew could be converted by letters. For they were prouder because of the royal dignity which was in the house of Ephraim.
31.1: 31.1 They broke the images, etc. After the coming of the Savior, not only in Jerusalem and in Judah, but in all the nations of the world idolatry was destroyed, and the pride of the devil fell. And as the number of the faithful increases, the worship of demons decreases, until at the end of the world the last death is swallowed up, and the Lord alone shall reign in that day.
32.4: 32.4 They stopped all. Against pagans and heretics who fight, diligent caution must be used, and the mysteries veiled, whence: Do not give what is holy to dogs, nor cast your pearls before swine.
32.5: 32.5 He built. RABANUS in Chronicles. Christ built the Church, which is the city of God, etc., down to and appointed teachers as princes of spiritual wars.
33.12: 33.12 And he did penance greatly before the God of his fathers. RABANUS. Having heard the repentance of Manasseh, no one ought to despair of the mercy of God, but rather through repentance presume on pardon.
34.5: 34.5 Moreover the bones. RABANUS. He burned the priests on the altars of the idols to show that their sacrifices were deadly, who not only offered victims of cattle to demons, but handed over men themselves to idolatry. This signifies all who, enslaved to the service of the devil, had ended a sacrilegious life in time, to be consumed with eternal torments, each according to his merit.
34.22: 34.22 To Huldah the prophetess, etc. JEROME. Huldah was the wife of Shallum, the uncle of the father of Jeremiah, and of the father of Hanamel. She dwelt in the second. It was a place in Jerusalem outside the wall of the city and the outer rampart, which was called the second: it is mentioned in the prophet Zephaniah.
35.1: 35.1 And Josiah kept in Jerusalem, etc. RABANUS. We are admonished first to cleanse the earth of our heart from all vices, and so to celebrate the Passover to the Lord, not with the old leaven, nor with the leaven of malice and wickedness, but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth, 1 Corinthians 5. Mystically, however, Josiah, that is strength of the Lord, signifies Christ, of whom it is read: The Lord strong and mighty: the Lord mighty in battle, Psalm 23. Josiah is also interpreted salvation of the Lord, and Christ saves his people from their sins, Matthew 1. By the zeal of God he cleanses the land of Judah and Jerusalem from all uncleannesses, who said through the prophet: The zeal of your house has eaten me up, Psalm 68. Of whom elsewhere: Whose fan is in his hand, and he will thoroughly cleanse his floor, Matthew 3. He celebrates the true Passover in the eighteenth year of his reign: because in the eighth age, the general resurrection being given, he leads his saints with the perfection of good works to the denary of eternal blessedness, all scandals having first been cast out of his kingdom.
35.3: 35.3 Put the ark in the sanctuary of the temple, which Solomon the son of David king of Israel built. The Hebrews relate that the ark was carried out of the temple in the time of Ahaz, the idols being sent into the temple by him, and was taken into the house of Shallum, husband of Huldah, uncle of Jeremiah. For it could not be together with idols.
35.18: 35.18 There was no Passover like this, etc. Because the figures being taken away on the day of judgment, the saints will pass from death to life, from corruption to glory, and in the sight of their Maker in the heavenly Jerusalem will rejoice forever: because the God of gods will be seen in Zion, because he has magnified his mercy in the fortified city.
35.21: 35.21 To which God. Because from the words of Jeremiah and the other prophets he could have known the will of the Lord, by which judgment was to be passed on the sinful people. Hence Rabshakeh also said of Sennacherib king of the Assyrians: The Lord commanded me to go up to the land, Psalm 83, because the prophets had foretold that he would go up, which was by no means hidden from him.
35.22: 35.22 In the plain of Megiddo. The killing of Josiah, who was killed by Pharaoh Necho at Megiddo, signifies the persecution of the ancient enemy against the preachers, whom he tries to put to death and remove from the Church, that he may more easily invade and scatter the whole people. For Pharaoh is interpreted scattering, Necho striking, Megiddo of temptation. The devil is indeed permitted to rise against the saints: and he strives with all his strength, by tempting to strike the flock of God, first removing by scattering those by whose comfort others fight against the enemy.
36.4: 36.4 And he appointed. Necho made Jehoiakim king, and laid a fine upon the land of a hundred talents of silver: because the devil exacts a tribute of service from the people of the lost, that they may be ready for his obedience as much in mind as in speech. And he turned. It is to be noted that of the same Jehoiakim son of Josiah it is written thus in Kings: Jehoiakim slept with his fathers, and Jehoiachin his son reigned in his place, 4 Kings 24. Josephus, however, says: When the king of Babylon had entered the city, he by no means kept faith, but killed the strongest and most beautiful young men together with King Jehoiakim, whom he commanded to be cast out unburied before the wall. His son Jehoiachin he made king over the whole province. Those who were appointed in dignities, to the number of three thousand, he led into Babylon, among whom was Ezekiel, still a boy. This was the end Jehoiakim the king had, who lived thirty years, and reigned eleven years. The successor of the kingdom of Jehoiakim, a king named Ononimus, reigned three months and ten days. It is to be known that when anyone has once enslaved himself to any vice, he will be subject to many masters. Hence Jehoiakim, whom Pharaoh had forced to pay tribute to him, Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon compels to serve him for three years. Nebuchadnezzar signifies the same as Pharaoh; namely the prince of confusion and ruler of these darknesses. When the devil forces anyone to pay him the tribute of sin, he reduces him wholly into his dominion, and exacts full service, namely by persuasion, delight, consent, also by thought, speech, and action. JEROME, Questions on Chronicles, vol. 3. It is to be known that the name of this Jehoiachin, etc., down to depraved by the examples of their superiors they yield with them to the prey of the devil.
36.10: 36.10 And the king. Zedekiah signifies those who take up rule among the people of God: for Zedekiah is interpreted just of the Lord. They receive the seat of justice to exercise works of justice, they receive the dignity of honor and office, especially because as sons of Josiah, that is of the salvation of the Lord, through the grace of baptism and the anointing of chrism they deserve to be named: but degenerating they fall back into the foulness of vices, and turn their subjects to impiety, neither keeping the faith they had promised to God, nor preserving covenants of peace with men. Such the divine law, the miracles of the prophets and apostles daily admonish to depart from sins and return to the Lord by penance: but once hardened they despise the words of salvation, whence God, angered, sends against them the king of the Chaldeans, that is the devil with his satellites, that is spiritual wickednesses, who sparing no age, deferring to no dignity, carry whomever they capture to Babylon, that is to confusion; and they burn the house of the Lord, because they force the faithful, who are the temple of God, to blaspheme. They destroy the walls of Jerusalem when they cast down the guards of the shepherds, burn the towers when they consume prelates with unlawful desires: they demolish everything precious when they reduce to nothing those who applaud themselves for the prerogative of virtue and knowledge. The end of the book of Chronicles is like the beginning of the book of the priest Ezra: hence what we expounded there, there is no need to repeat here. Of Cyrus also, how he signifies Christ, and what is said of him, and what refers to him, we expounded in Isaiah. RABANUS, from Bede. Solomon built the temple of the Lord in seven years in Jerusalem, etc., down to namely and of the city of God from which they had been cast out, they receive.
